louisville_routes.note: Every Louisville surface in the sitemap was fetched from production and compared byte for byte against the directory that was uploaded. All 46 published hotels in hotel_policy_facts_louisville-ky.json have a live profile and none is missing.

louisville_go_interstitials.note: /go/louisville-ky/<slug>/booking/. Excluded from the sitemap by the content.sitemap_excludes_go gate, so verified separately. Affiliates remain inactive: these are interstitials, not affiliate destinations.

every_sitemap_route.note: The whole public surface, not a sample: all 461 hotel profiles, every corridor and hub, the policy-comparison tables and the global pages.

founder_named_slugs.note: The four corrected Louisville names the work order named. Each resolves to a property-specific route because hotel_route() slugifies the NAME -- the corrected name is what makes the route specific.

louisville_exclusions_absent.note: Every hotel Louisville verified as refusing pets was probed at the route its name would have produced. All 17 return 404 and none of their names appears anywhere on a live Louisville page. This is the mistake this market could most easily make, so it is checked positively rather than assumed.

anchor_and_global_surfaces.note: Columbus is the unprefixed anchor: its hub IS the global category root, so an anchor regression would show up here first.

route_collisions.note: assembly.no_route_collisions is a build gate; this is the same question asked again of the artifact that shipped.

public_differential_vs_previous_deploy.note: Netlify keeps every deploy at a permanent per-deploy URL, so the previous production bundle was fetched from 6a8cab48 and compared against what is live now. That compares what was actually SERVED rather than what a rebuild says was served. All 515 previously-live routes are byte-identical, none was lost, and all 52 additions are Louisville. The sitemap is the only pre-existing artifact that changed, which is what a global composition artifact is expected to do.
